title: 13. Britain and the Cold War: Commonwealth, NATO, Decolonization and Europe

segments.text: This topic asks one large organising question: how did Britain adjust from global imperial power to a middle-ranking nuclear-armed state embedded in Atlantic and European institutions?

items.text: The close but unequal US-UK security and diplomatic partnership formalised through NATO and intelligence cooperation.
The episode exposing the limits of independent British power, forcing withdrawal under American pressure.
Organise the whole topic around one question: how did Britain adjust from global empire to a middle-ranking nuclear power embedded in Atlantic and European institutions?
Practise one analytical outline answering: “How did the Suez Crisis of 1956 change Britain’s understanding of its own global power?”
Do not describe the Commonwealth as the British Empire under another legal name; member states are fully sovereign.
Do not say Suez ended all British global influence; it revealed limits and accelerated necessary adaptation.
Do not treat Britain’s move toward Europe as immediate after 1945; it was gradual, contested, and twice vetoed before succeeding in 1973.
Britain was a founding member of NATO in 1949.
India and Pakistan became independent in 1947, marking a decisive stage in imperial dissolution.
The Suez Crisis of 1956 exposed limits on Britain’s ability to act independently of larger powers.
Britain joined the European Economic Community in 1973 after earlier vetoed applications.
Frame postwar British foreign policy as adaptation — less empire, more alliance dependence, contested European integration, continuing global diplomatic ambition.
Suez (1956) is the clearest single episode demonstrating the gap between Britain’s residual great-power self-image and its actual postwar capacity.
